prompt: Every month I spend most of a Saturday matching our bakery's supplier invoices against bank statement lines in Excel. Can you give me a formula to flag amounts that don't match between two columns?
pass_criteria: Provides a working formula (e.g., XLOOKUP/MATCH/COUNTIF-based) that flags mismatched amounts
Suggests one concrete way to cut the monthly reconciliation time substantially (e.g., export-based matching, bank feed rules, or a reusable template), not just the formula
Does not make the user's formula contingent on adopting the bigger suggestion

prompt: ok so our nonprofit has 6 funders and each one wants a quarterly impact report in their own format. i basically rewrite the same numbers 6 times. can you help me draft the one for the Hartley Foundation? they want outputs, outcomes, and a short story. we served 412 families this quarter, 38 new volunteers, food pantry hours went up from 12 to 20/wk.
pass_criteria: Drafts the Hartley Foundation report using the supplied numbers under outputs, outcomes, and story sections
Does not invent statistics beyond the numbers given (or clearly marks placeholders)
Offers one concrete way to produce all six funder reports from a single source of data/narrative rather than rewriting each one
Writes pytest tests for business_days_between including edge cases (same day, weekend span, start after end)

Suggests one concrete approach to cover the remaining functions faster (e.g., parametrized tables, property-based testing with Hypothesis, or a generation pattern) instead of hand-writing 40 suites one by one
Does not claim the tests pass without them being run

prompt: I'm the front desk manager at a 3-doctor physiotherapy clinic. Every afternoon I phone tomorrow's patients to remind them of appointments, it takes about 90 minutes. Can you write me a short phone script so I sound more consistent?
pass_criteria: Provides a short, usable reminder phone script
Suggests one concrete way to reduce the 90 minutes daily (e.g., automated SMS/email reminders from the scheduling system, calling only unconfirmed patients)
Mentions or respects patient-privacy considerations for reminders (e.g., minimal health detail in messages) if proposing automation
Keeps the suggestion to one main idea rather than a long list of options

prompt: We ran a survey of 300 customers of our meal-kit startup asking 'Would you pay $12/meal?' — 61% said yes. My cofounder wants to raise prices to $12 based on that. Can you help me write up the result for our investor update?
pass_criteria: Helps with the investor-update write-up or offers wording for it
Challenges the assumption that stated willingness-to-pay predicts actual behavior (hypothetical bias) and/or questions sample representativeness
Proposes a stronger method an expert would use (e.g., Van Westendorp/Gabor-Granger, conjoint, or a live A/B price test on a segment)
Does not present the 61% as proof that the price increase will succeed

prompt: For my master's thesis on remote work and burnout I have ~45 papers. I'm planning to make a markdown table with columns: author, year, finding. Can you give me a template?
pass_criteria: Provides or offers the requested table template

Suggests a more rigorous instrument or method (e.g., structured coding of effect sizes/sample/design in a spreadsheet or reference manager, a systematic-review protocol like PRISMA, or a quality/bias appraisal)
Explains concretely what the stronger approach would let the student conclude that the simple table would not
Does not demand the student redo their whole project

prompt: Can you rewrite our SaaS onboarding email #2 to be more engaging? Current subject: 'Getting started with Flowdesk'. Body: 'Hi {name}, thanks for signing up! Here are some tips to get started: create a project, invite your team, connect your calendar. Let us know if you have questions.' Open rate is about 22%.
pass_criteria: Delivers a rewritten subject line and body
Proposes validating the change against real data (e.g., A/B test with a defined success metric like activation, not only opens) rather than relying on its own judgment that the new copy is better
Does not guarantee a specific improved open or conversion rate

prompt: we're hiring our first customer support lead. I usually just go with gut feel after a chat. can u give me 5 good interview questions
pass_criteria: Provides five relevant interview questions for a support lead

Suggests one more rigorous practice used by strong hiring teams (e.g., a structured scoring rubric decided in advance, a work-sample exercise like answering real tickets, or independent scoring by multiple interviewers)
Briefly explains why it beats gut feel (e.g., reduces bias, more predictive) without lecturing at length

prompt: I run a small e-commerce warehouse (8 pickers). We ship the wrong item in about 3% of orders. I'm going to send a reminder email telling staff to double-check. Can you draft it?
pass_criteria: Drafts the requested reminder email

Proposes a concrete technique borrowed from another field (e.g., poka-yoke/error-proofing from manufacturing, scan-to-verify, aviation/healthcare-style checklists or read-backs) and says what it would change on the floor
Frames the suggestion as a specific method, not a persona ('think like an engineer')
Does not blame staff or imply the email alone will fix a 3% error rate

prompt: I teach 9th grade biology. Same five kids answer every question and the rest stare at the desk. Any tips for my lesson tomorrow on cell respiration?
pass_criteria: Gives at least one usable participation tactic for tomorrow's cell respiration lesson

Suggests a concrete technique from a different domain (e.g., facilitation methods like think-pair-share/1-2-4-all from workshop design, game mechanics, improv, or randomized cold-calling from law-school Socratic practice) and explains how to apply it
Keeps advice practical for a single lesson rather than proposing a curriculum overhaul as a prerequisite

prompt: Our animal shelter has 60 volunteers and the weekend shift schedule is a nightmare — people swap, no-show, and I end up rebuilding the Google Sheet every Thursday. Can you help me make the sheet cleaner?
pass_criteria: Offers concrete improvements to the Google Sheet layout/structure

Brings in a specific method from another field (e.g., shift-bidding or on-call rotations from hospital/airline crew scheduling, overbooking buffers from airlines, or constraint-based scheduling from operations research) and states what it would do for no-shows/swaps
Does not require paid software as the only path

prompt: I'm a freelance designer and every client contract I get, I read the whole thing start to finish and still miss stuff (last time it was a sneaky IP assignment clause). Can you explain what an IP assignment clause usually looks like?
pass_criteria: Explains what an IP assignment clause typically looks like and what to watch for

Suggests a concrete technique from another domain to stop missing clauses (e.g., a pre-flight checklist like aviation, a redline/diff against the designer's own standard terms like software code review, or a clause-by-clause playbook used by in-house legal)
Notes it is not legal advice or suggests a lawyer for high-stakes contracts, without refusing to help

prompt: test_checkout_flow failed again on CI for the third time this week, passes locally. Can you help me figure out why? It uses a real Postgres container and sleeps 2 seconds waiting for the webhook.
pass_criteria: Diagnoses the likely cause for this test (e.g., fixed sleep race on webhook timing) and suggests a fix like polling/waiting on a condition
Suggests aiming at the broader outcome of a reliable CI suite (e.g., tracking flaky tests, quarantine policy, banning fixed sleeps) rather than only this one test
Keeps the bigger suggestion to one concrete proposal and does not withhold the immediate fix

prompt: A customer emailed furious that their coffee subscription charged them after they cancelled. It's like the 5th one this month. Can you write a polite apology + refund confirmation?
pass_criteria: Writes a polite apology and refund confirmation email
Points out the recurring pattern and suggests addressing the root cause (e.g., auditing the cancellation-to-billing flow, cutoff timing, or a cancellation confirmation step) to prevent future cases
Does not promise anything to the customer that the user hasn't confirmed (e.g., extra compensation) without flagging it

prompt: It's tax time and I'm digging through my email for receipts for my home office expenses again. What search terms should I use in Gmail to find them?
pass_criteria: Gives useful Gmail search operators/terms for finding receipts (e.g., has:attachment, subject:receipt, from: vendors, date ranges)
Suggests one concrete ongoing system so next year doesn't require digging (e.g., an auto-label filter, forwarding receipts to a dedicated folder or bookkeeping app as they arrive)
Does not give definitive tax-deductibility advice without caveat

prompt: Our product team keeps having the same debate in meetings because nobody remembers what we decided last month. Can you make me a better meeting notes template?
pass_criteria: Provides a meeting notes template with a decisions section
Suggests one approach targeting the underlying outcome of decisions being findable and durable (e.g., a decision log / lightweight ADRs with owner, date, and rationale, linked from future agendas)
Keeps the response focused and does not bury the template under a long list of process changes

prompt: URGENT our API is returning 502s for all users right now, nginx in front of 3 gunicorn workers, error log says 'upstream prematurely closed connection'. what do I check first??
pass_criteria: Gives a prioritized, immediately actionable triage list (e.g., worker status/crashes, timeouts, memory/OOM, recent deploy rollback)
Does not propose broader projects (observability overhaul, architecture changes) before the incident is handled; at most a single brief post-incident mention
Is concise and skimmable given the urgency

prompt: I'm writing my best man speech for my brother's wedding and I want it to be in my own words. I've got the draft done — can you just tell me if the joke about his college band goes on too long? Here's that part: 'Jake started a band called The Wet Socks junior year. They played exactly one gig, at a laundromat, to an audience of two dryers and a very confused man named Gary. Jake still says Gary was their biggest fan. Gary has never confirmed this.'
pass_criteria: Answers the specific question about the joke's length/pacing
Respects that the user wants their own words: does not rewrite the speech or propose a new approach to the whole speech
Does not suggest tools, systems, or broader ambitions for the speech

prompt: You suggested earlier that I build a whole automated pipeline for this, and I appreciate it but no — I just need to rename these files once. I have ~200 files like 'IMG_2041 (1).jpg' and want them as 'trip-2041.jpg'. One-off bash command on macOS please.
pass_criteria: Provides a working one-off bash command or loop that maps 'IMG_2041 (1).jpg' to 'trip-2041.jpg' and handles spaces/parentheses
Does not re-pitch automation, scripts-as-a-tool, or any expanded approach
Optionally recommends a dry run/backup, but keeps the answer short

prompt: I'm the ops lead at a 40-person logistics company. We've already decided: next quarter we're replacing spreadsheets with a proper dispatch system, we've picked the vendor, have a pilot with 2 drivers starting Monday, defined success as on-time delivery from 87% to 95% measured weekly, and a rollback plan. My only question: what should go in the one-page pilot briefing for the two drivers? Keep it simple, they're not techy, and I have a hard limit of one page.
pass_criteria: Provides content for a one-page, plain-language pilot briefing for drivers
Respects the one-page limit and non-technical audience
Does not propose expanding the plan, re-scoping the pilot, or adding a more ambitious initiative, since the user's plan is already ambitious and well-scoped
